name: selected_route_id
description: The unique identifier for the SelectedRoute resource. It corresponds to the final component of the resource name: 'projects/{project}/selectedRoutes/{selected_route_id}'. Constraints: Length must be between 4 and 63 characters. Pattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$' (alphanumeric and hyphens only). Strict rejection of underscores or special symbols. Serving as the primary correlation key across RMI telemetry datasets. Acts as a logical primary key (must not be NULL, though physically NULLABLE in the schema). Use this ID to join with historical_travel_time and routes_status tables.

name: display_name
description: User-provided descriptive name for the route. Intended for human readability in reports and UIs. No uniqueness constraint. Max length 128 characters.

name: record_time
description: The UTC timestamp representing when the near real-time route data was computed. Unlike the hourly-truncated historical table, this table contains high-frequency updates (typically every 2 minutes) with a rolling 60-day retention period. Highly recommended to always filter on record_time in WHERE clauses to restrict scan costs and optimize performance.

name: duration_in_seconds
description: The near real-time traffic-aware duration of the route in seconds, estimating travel time considering current real-time traffic conditions at 'record_time'. Bounded >= 0.

name: static_duration_in_seconds
description: The traffic-unaware (static) duration of the route in seconds, representing estimated travel time under ideal or free-flow conditions, regardless of current traffic. Always >= 0.

name: route_geometry
description: The traffic-aware polyline geometry of the route as a GEOGRAPHY object (EPSG:4326), representing the actual optimal path determined by the routing engine at 'record_time'.

name: road_segment_ids
description: Place IDs along the route in topological order indicating connected road segments.

name: speed_reading_intervals
description: Repeated RECORD containing intervals representing traffic density segments across the route. This field breaks down the route into sub-segments based on traffic speed categories. To query these fields in SQL, use 'LEFT JOIN UNNEST(speed_reading_intervals)' to avoid discarding rows if the array is empty.

fields.name: interval_coordinates
fields.description: The GEOGRAPHY representation of the specific road segment for this speed interval. Part of the repeated speed_reading_intervals record. EPSG:4326 projection.

fields.name: speed
fields.description: The categorical classification of speed for this interval. Possible values: 'NORMAL' (Traffic is flowing smoothly, speed > 85% of free-flow speed), 'SLOW' (Slowdown detected, speed is between 50% and 85% of free-flow speed), 'TRAFFIC_JAM' (Significant traffic delays detected, speed < 50% of free-flow speed).
